answers.collision_check: Against retire's charter (ticket 750ead1af9c1; why: delete code only after measuring in the same act that nothing calls it): a false namer never makes retire unsafe, only slower and its report wrong, so narrowing to true namers serves the same why — a distinction, not a collision. Against Law 3: the report's 'callers'/'namers' lists are measurements; false entries are a wrong measurement, which this fixes.

Horizon: re-read when a retire reports a caller that does not name the target.
answers.gates_bound: code-seam's gate-set: the tester's proof gate (red-first proof sealed red, then green after the build), hollow evidence at PROVED, feeds back to origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8).
answers.missing_check: The dotted needle needs the same boundary: 'cairn.devices.cc.superclaude' must not hit 'cairn.devices.cc.superclaude_py' or 'cairn.devices.cc.superclaude.x'? — a dotted module followed by '.<ident>' IS a submodule reference, which for a package target is a real caller; for a file target there is no submodule. Decided: '.' followed by an identifier char is not a boundary for either needle (a file target can have no submodules, a directory target's submodule references are caught by the directory path needle 'pkg/' plus its own files' needles). Nothing else asserted-wrapped is open.
